gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-arme: Friendly and striking, Lemon Milk spaces its rounded letters wide, like a rolling-ball pen trail. Noto Serif Armenian gives big, open counters with mild stroke contrast, so paragraphs unfold in a traditional, assured tone.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-dogr: Noto Serif Dogra feels bookish, its capitals only slightly taller than lowercase. Lemon Milk draws wide, compass-round letters up top, while the body's faint crayon-like rhythm lets long paragraphs feel soft and unhurried.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-guja: Lemon Milk spreads friendly, rounded letters wide apart, each one traced in a single pencil-like line. Lemon Milk grabs attention; Noto Serif Gujarati settles quietly into bookish, authoritative paragraphs.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-otto: Lemon Milk is the headline voice, a constant-width outline you could trace with a finger. Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq is the dignified one, built for text, with bowls that swell only slightly and crossbars a touch thinner.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-telu: Wide, round and friendly, Lemon Milk grabs the eye with uniform strokes. Noto Serif Telugu does the refined, traditional work, its thick strokes only slightly heavier than thin ones, its tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-thai: Loose, rounded, unshaded: Lemon Milk makes a friendly, striking headline. Noto Serif Thai sits beneath with big bodies and barely showing ascenders, a mellow, bookish classic serif that gives the headline room.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-tibe: One pen-trail line, loose and wide, gives Lemon Milk its friendly, rounded look. Noto Serif Tibetan then takes over with gentle joins, x-height rising near cap height, and an authoritative, literary voice.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-fs-spline-sans: Minecraftia lingers on every character, one beat each, with a towering lowercase. Spline Sans moves in underneath with a moderate lowercase and uniform strokes, keeping things approachable and contemporary.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-gf-fanwood-text: Heavy stems, hair-thin arms: Minecraftia is pure, familiar fun. Fanwood Text takes the literary reading, its large-eyed lowercase and gentle curves rewarding a close look, while Minecraftia does the loud display work.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-gf-manuale: Lopsided weights, towering lowercase: Minecraftia is familiar fun. It earns its keep big and short, while Manuale brings traditional, editorial steadiness through a large-eyed lowercase and moderate contrast.
